# Conservation Testing {.unnumbered}

*A budget is only as trustworthy as the conservation of the quantities that feed
it. This chapter sets out the step-by-step checks we use to test and cross-check
that a SCHISM-AED budget is accurate — what can go wrong, how to benchmark each
term, and what we have learned from applying the checks to the Pioneer runs.*

The checks below are implemented as diagnostic scripts in
[`analytics/pioneer_region_flux/diagnostics/`](../../../analytics/pioneer_region_flux/diagnostics/).
They target a run **by name** via `run_config.py`, so the same check runs against
002 or 003 without editing paths:

```bash
python diagnostics/conservation_check.py --run 003 --days 14
```

`active_run()` resolves `--run` / `--run-dir` / `SCHISM_RUN` (default 002) and
`--days`; the `RunConfig` derives all run-file paths, parses the start date from
`param.nml`, and reads `n_regions` from `fluxflag.prop`.

## Problems and issues in mass conservation

Before trusting a budget it helps to know where conservation can break down in a
coupled hydrodynamic–biogeochemical model. The recurring culprits are:

- **Source injection into small or dry cells.** A point source adds volume and
  mass to its receiving element each step. If the injected volume is large
  relative to the cell volume — a high injection ratio
  $\mathrm{rat}=Q\,\Delta t/\mathrm{bigv}$ — or the cell is intermittently dry,
  not all of the intended mass is retained.
- **Untracked boundary transport.** `flux.out` only records transport across
  edges where adjacent `fluxflag.prop` values differ by exactly 1 (and neither is
  −1). Any control-volume perimeter that does not meet this rule is invisible to
  the boundary term.
- **Tidal cancellation.** At a tidal gate the net transport is a small residual
  between large flood and ebb excursions, so sign and magnitude errors are easy
  to hide.
- **Coupling / numerical loss.** In principle a tracer could be lost in the
  AED ↔ SCHISM hand-off or in transport; this must be ruled out before blaming
  the budget terms.

The remaining sections are the checks that isolate each of these.

## Conservation benchmarking of AED variables

**Theory.** A conservative tracer (no sources, sinks or reactions inside the
domain) must be conserved exactly bar boundary exchange. Comparing a tracer
carried by AED against one carried natively by SCHISM, with identical forcing,
isolates whether any loss is in the **AED coupling** or in the **shared
transport**.

**What we find.** `TRC_tr1` (AED) and `GEN_1` (SCHISM-native) are injected
identically and evolve bit-for-bit together — so transport is conservative and
the AED hand-off is not losing mass. This is the decisive first benchmark: it
moves attention away from the biogeochemistry and onto the source and boundary
terms.

![Conservative-tracer benchmark: AED `TRC_tr1` vs SCHISM-native `GEN_1`. Identical evolution rules out an AED coupling loss. Source: `…/diagnostics/tr1_vs_gen1_compare.py`](../../assets/images/budget/tr1_vs_gen1_compare.png){#fig-tr1-gen1}

## flux.out region transect assessment

**Theory.** The boundary term (E) is read entirely from `flux.out` at the
control-volume transect — for the Pioneer CV, the **(3↔2) mouth gate**. Its
accuracy depends on (i) whether the flagged transect actually covers the whole
perimeter, (ii) the sign/direction convention, and (iii) how the raw
positive/negative components are combined.

**What we find.** Classifying every edge around the perimeter shows that a large
part of the mouth is **untracked** — transport leaves through edges `flux.out`
never sees.

![Edge classification at the mouth: tracked (counted in `flux.out`) vs untracked perimeter edges. Source: `…/diagnostics/mouth_edge_classification.py`](../../assets/images/budget/mouth_edge_classification.png){#fig-mouth-edges}

Reconstructing the flux directly from model velocity × layer thickness on each
mouth edge, and comparing against `flux.out`, recovers the missing transport —
confirming the gap is a `fluxflag` **coverage** issue, not a model error, and
checking the directionality of the reported sign.

![Independent edge-flux reconstruction vs the `flux.out` transect. Source: `…/diagnostics/edge_flux_reconstruction.py`](../../assets/images/budget/edge_flux_reconstruction.png){#fig-edge-recon}

Looking at the **raw** gate signal shows why care is needed: the net is a small
residual between large, near-cancelling flood/ebb excursions. Separating the
positive and negative components keeps that explicit.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Positive / negative / net breakdown at the (2↔3) gate. Source: `…/diagnostics/check_flux_upwind.py`](../../assets/images/budget/flux_pos_neg_breakdown.png){#fig-posneg}

![Raw cumulative `flux.out` components. Source: `…/diagnostics/plot_flux_raw.py`](../../assets/images/budget/flux_raw_pos_neg_net.png){#fig-fluxraw}
:::

This tidal cancellation is also why run 003 holds the tide flat for the first 14
days ([the flat-tide method](../part2-model-setup/07-boundary-and-tidal-forcing.qmd)):
with the excursions removed, the source term can be assessed on its own.

## Volume conservation

**Theory.** Before any *tracer* budget can be trusted, the control volume must
conserve **water**: the change in CV water volume must equal what enters minus
what leaves. With the [control volume](15-pioneer-estuary.qmd) closed on the
mouth transect, that is the realised river inflow plus the net volume flux across
the mouth,
$$\Delta V(t) = \int Q_\text{src}\,r(t)\,\alpha\,dt \;+\; \int q_\text{mouth}\,dt .$$
Three subtleties matter. (i) The **realised** source differs from the raw
`vsource.th`. SCHISM eases each source on over a startup window with the ramp
$r(t)=\tanh\!\big(2t/(86400\,\texttt{dramp\_ss})\big)$ (`dramp_ss = 10` d), so the
input is below the prescribed value for the first ~10 days; and a small empirical
factor $\alpha$ (`--source-realisation-factor`, default **0.96**) captures a
residual *flow-proportional* source-volume loss at the tiny (210 m²) src3 cell —
the volume analogue of the small-cell `rat`-dilution (§Inflow source mass
assessment). $\alpha$ is applied **only** to the source term.
(ii) Precipitation−evaporation would otherwise appear as a volume source, but
run 003 sets `isconsv = 0`, so the precip/evap volume flux is switched off
(`schism_step.F90`, the `(precip-evap)` term is inside an `isconsv/=0` block) —
it is **not** a term in this budget. (iii) The storage integral counts only
*actively-wet* water: SCHISM's wetting/drying scheme keeps a thin residual column
(order `h0 = 0.01` m) on cells it flags dry, and that numerically-dormant "dead
water" would otherwise slosh in and out of $\Delta V$ as the intertidal margin
wets and dries. We exclude it by masking on SCHISM's own `dryFlagNode`
(zeroing dry nodes' layer thicknesses in `load_zcoord_dz`), so the integral
follows the model's own wet/dry bookkeeping rather than re-deciding it.

**What we find.** Over the **14-day flat-tide window** the budget closes to
**−0.5 % of throughput** with the realised source (ramp × α = 0.96); the raw
`vsource.th` leaves it ~28 % open, and ramp-only (α = 1) leaves ~−4 %. That ~−4 %
ramp-only residual **correlates with river inflow at r = −0.93** (≈4 % of the
river volume) — i.e. it is a flow-proportional *source* loss, which is exactly
what the small α corrects, and being source-side it propagates cleanly to
river-borne tracer budgets via the known river concentration. Over the **full
~53 days a residual of ~−9 % remains** (−12.5 % with α = 1), and *this* part is
**real and accumulating** — averaging out the tidal swing, the daily-mean
residual trends monotonically through the tidal phase rather than oscillating
about zero, and (unlike the flat-tide part) is **river-uncorrelated** (r = +0.07).
α is deliberately *not* raised to force 53-day closure: that would mis-attribute
the tidal mouth-flux error to the rivers.

It is, however, **not a model volume leak**: the whole-domain volume
(`total.out`) conserves to **+0.3 %** on a tidal-mean basis (it oscillates by
±2.2×10⁹ m³ with the tide but its mean is unchanged). Nor is it
**dead-water over-counting**: masking the ~17 % of node-samples SCHISM flags dry
(subtlety iii) shifts the residual by <0.2 %, because that water is present at
both ends and cancels in $\Delta V$. The accumulation is instead a limitation of
the **CV budget under active tides**: `flux.out` is a per-step *velocity-based
reconstruction* of the transect flux, not bit-identical to the model's internal
semi-implicit continuity flux, and the CV volume itself swings by ±153 % of its
mean each tidal cycle — so a sub-percent per-cycle mismatch between the diagnostic
flux and the true continuity accumulates over ~70 cycles. With the tide held flat there is no such
flux to accumulate, which is why the **flat-tide window is the clean test** and
why run 003 was designed that way. The flat-tide closure (~96 %) confirms the
control-volume geometry and mouth tracking are sound; the much larger salt and
nitrogen gaps are *tracer-side* (source-injection loss, §Inflow source mass
assessment), not a control-volume leak — but the **tidal-phase volume residual is
a genuine, if modest, accounting limitation, not numerical noise**.

![Pioneer CV water-volume conservation (top: 14-day flat-tide window; bottom: full ~53 days). Black = observed ΔV; green = predicted from realised source (ramp × α=0.96) + mouth flux; grey dotted = raw `vsource.th` (over-open); orange = residual (≈0 on the flat-tide window; the ~−9% under tides is the flux-diagnostic bracket). Source: `…/diagnostics/volume_conservation_proof.py`](../../assets/images/budget/volume_conservation_003.png){#fig-vol-cons}

**Confirming the cause — an independent mouth-flux reconstruction.** To test
whether the tidal-phase residual lies in the `flux.out` *flux diagnostic* rather
than in the storage, the mouth volume flux was rebuilt independently from node
velocities (`horizontalVelX/Y`) and the **same `zCoordinates` layer thicknesses
used by the storage integral** (not `ENV_layer_ht`), summed over the 14 flag-2↔3
gate edges (`edge_flux_zcoord_check.py`). Over the flat-tide window the two agree
to **0.1 %** (−2.92 vs −2.92 ×10⁷ m³), so there the residual is unambiguously the
source ramp, not the gate. Under active tides they **diverge by ~33 %**
(`flux.out` −3.67 vs reconstruction −4.87 ×10⁷ m³), and the resulting volume
residuals **straddle zero** — −12.7 % using `flux.out`, +15.1 % using the
reconstruction (@fig-edge-flux). Two independent velocity-based estimates of the
*same* gate bracketing closure from opposite sides is the signature of a
**flux-diagnostic limitation at a tidally-energetic, partially-wet gate**: the
true continuity flux lies between them and closes the budget. The storage term is
exact and not implicated, consistent with the global +0.3 % volume conservation.

![Mouth volume flux — `flux.out` col 3 (diagnostic) vs an independent reconstruction (node velocities × `zCoordinates` `dz`, consistent with the storage integral). Left: cumulative flux — identical under flat tide, diverging ~33 % once the tide is active. Right: the two volume-budget residuals straddle zero, locating the tidal-phase discrepancy in the flux diagnostic, not the storage. Source: `…/diagnostics/edge_flux_zcoord_check.py`](../../assets/images/budget/edge_flux_zcoord_53d.png){#fig-edge-flux}

## Inflow source mass assessment

**Theory.** A point source should add exactly $Q\,c\,\Delta t$ of tracer mass per
step. Whether it does depends on the receiving cell: a high injection ratio
`rat` or a dry/near-dry cell means the model cannot accommodate the full
injection and mass is under-applied.

**What we find.** At the Pioneer River source the pulse drives a mean
$\mathrm{rat}\approx 7$ in a shallow, intermittently dry cell, implying only a
fraction of the intended mass is retained per step — a genuine source-side loss,
separate from the boundary issue above.

![Source-cell diagnostics: dry fraction, column depth, injection ratio `rat`, and implied per-step retention. Source: `…/diagnostics/src3_dry_rat_check.py`](../../assets/images/budget/src3_dry_rat_check.png){#fig-src3-rat}

## Flow connectivity assessment

**Theory.** Source-cell problems are tied to the wider question of whether the
upper river stays hydraulically connected. If the channel dries to disconnected
pools over the tidal cycle, both the source injection and the transport of its
load become unreliable.

**What we find.** The upper river is shallow and the wet channel narrows and
widens with the tide, intermittently isolating the reach around the source — the
context for the high `rat` above.

![Upper-river bathymetry and wet/dry connectivity. Source: `…/archive/upper_river_connectivity.py`](../../assets/images/setup/upper_river_connectivity.png){#fig-connectivity-ct}

{{< video ../../assets/videos/upper_river_connectivity.mp4 >}}

*Upper-river water depth over the tidal cycle (red = dry). Source:
`analytics/animations/upper_river_connectivity_animation.py`.*

## Per variable region accounts

**Theory.** The previous checks focus on conservative quantities; the final step
is to account for **every** state variable over the region — cumulative source
input, tracked transect flux, and control-volume vs domain-integrated mass —
side by side, so reactive variables can be sanity-checked too.

**What we find.** `per_variable_plots.py` renders this three-panel account for
all 20 variables. A few representative panels:

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![`TRC_tr1`](../../assets/images/budget/per_variable/TRC_tr1.png){#fig-pv-trc1}

![`GEN_1`](../../assets/images/budget/per_variable/GEN_1.png){#fig-pv-gen1}

![`NIT_amm`](../../assets/images/budget/per_variable/NIT_amm.png){#fig-pv-nitamm}
:::

The full set is produced by the script into the run's `_outputs/` directory.

## Diagnostics reference

| Script | Check |
|---|---|
| `tr1_vs_gen1_compare.py` | conservative-tracer benchmark (AED vs SCHISM) |
| `mouth_edge_classification.py` / `cv_perimeter_tracked.py` | which mouth edges `flux.out` tracks |
| `edge_flux_reconstruction.py` | independent flux across the mouth vs `flux.out` |
| `edge_flux_zcoord_check.py` | mouth flux from node vel × `zCoordinates` dz (storage-consistent); brackets `flux.out` under tides |
| `check_flux_upwind.py` / `plot_flux_raw.py` | raw POS/NEG/NET gate breakdown |
| `src3_dry_rat_check.py` | source injection-ratio / dry-cell loss |
| `upper_river_connectivity.py` | upper-river wet/dry connectivity |
| `conservation_check.py` / `global_balance.py` | per-variable residual / boundary closure |
| `cv_definition_map.py` | control-volume definition map (cells, sources, transect) |
| `volume_conservation_proof.py` | CV water-volume closure (ramp-corrected) |
| `per_variable_plots.py` | 20-variable region accounts |

Earlier one-off scripts are retained under
`pioneer_region_flux/archive/` for the record.
